name: Ciarán Walsh
headline: 36, backend engineer, Galway
title: A Missing Saw
situation: It is Friday morning, just after dawn, and Ciarán is in the shed, packing his rucksack for his weekly repair of the footbridge step. He reaches for the handsaw he keeps on the hook by the door, but it is not there—only a bent hacksaw. He stands still for a moment, thinking. The hardware store opens at eight and is a ten-minute walk; he has a nine o'clock video call for work. He could buy a new handsaw and still make it to the bridge before the call, but he would have to skip his usual coffee. Or he could use the hacksaw, which is slower and less precise, but the step would still be mended. The morning is calm, and the mist is low over the marsh.

context.relationship_profiles:
The hardware store owner has served him for years and never asks what he buys.
His work team lead depends on his 9am call but knows nothing of his shed or bridge.
context.tendencies:
When a shed tool has gone missing, he has improvised with what hung nearby rather than break routine.
He has delayed a repair when the right tool was essential for a clean cut.
He has skipped his morning coffee on tight Fridays to keep both the repair and the work call.
context.current_state:
He is well-rested and calm, with the usual Friday purpose.
He has not yet had his first coffee, which he sips as he walks.
He feels only a mild irritation at the empty hook.
context.immediate_memories:
The empty hook recalls a borrowed handsaw he let a neighbour use to cut a branch two weeks ago.
The bent hacksaw reminds him of a rusted shackle last winter that he forced through it.
The low marsh mist brings back a rainy Friday when he fitted a step and stayed to check his nails.
context.reflective_memories:
His father believed the wrong tool costs twice the work, yet trusted one old hammer for everything.
He rushed one repair with a hacksaw and had to redo it when the cut cracked.
He has always thought a job done cleanly beats a quick one, but he also keeps his own schedule without asking help.
